features.headline: How Harry Kane rose to win Ballon d'Or and become an England legend
features.desc: Harry Kane went from overlooked youngster to Ballon d'Or winner. Now he's about to become England's record appearance-holder — and possibly their greatest-ever player.
body: Another week, another landmark moment for Harry Kane. Life is like that right now for the England captain, who will become his country's all-time record appearance-maker when leading out the Three Lions against Croatia on Thursday.

It completes a remarkable fortnight for Kane, 33, after he won the men's Ballon d'Or for the first time and signed a new contract with Bayern Munich through to 2029. He is now one of the highest-paid players in Europe, at more than €30 million per year.

Surpassing Peter Shilton's 125-cap England record felt almost impossible for more than three decades, especially for an outfield player. Wayne Rooney reached 120, David Beckham 115, Steven Gerrard 114 and Ashley Cole 107, but Kane will go clear on his own with years still ahead of him.

- Kane's long road to Ballon d'Or glory ends with crowning moment - USMNT or Manchester United: Pros and cons of Pochettino's options - Think less, run more: The rise of man-marking in the Premier League

England's goal-scoring record appeared a similarly difficult climb. Sir Bobby Charlton's tally of 49 stood for 45 years before Rooney reached the half-century in 2015 and later ended on 53. Kane is on a remarkable 91 — and counting.

He has captained England more often than any other player in history, leading England to back-to-back European Championship finals and a third-place finish at this summer's World Cup, the men's national team's best placing since their sole 1966 triumph.

The only thing missing is a major international trophy, something he willingly admits he would trade every individual accolade to have. But Kane's case for becoming England's greatest-ever player grows with each passing season.

features.headline: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes announce baby No. 4 on NFL trade deadline day
features.desc: The couple shared the news on a busy trade deadline day that also brought receiver Josh Downs to Kansas City.
body: Trade deadline day in the NFL brought additions on and off the field for Patrick Mahomes.

The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback and his wife, Brittany, announced Tuesday in a joint Instagram post that they are expecting their fourth child. The couple shared beachside family photos featuring their three children in the announcement.
"Another blessing from God... & then there were 6," they wrote with accompanying emojis.

The announcement means another sibling for daughters Sterling Skye, 5, and Golden Raye, 1, and son Patrick "Bronze" Lavon Mahomes III, 3. Patrick and Brittany were high school sweethearts in Texas before getting married in Hawaii in March 2022.

The family announcement capped a busy day for Mahomes, who also welcomed a new teammate in Kansas City. Earlier Tuesday, the Chiefs acquired wide receiver Josh Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick from the Indianapolis Colts for fourth- and fifth-round selections.

features.headline: Who will win MVP? Cy Young? Picks, analysis for 2026 MLB awards week
features.desc: Baseball's best players and managers of 2026 collect their hardware this week.
body: The baseball offseason has felt pretty normal so far if you can put the overhanging labor negotiations out of your mind.
Some of that normalcy comes from the gradual easing into the initial phases of the hot stove season — contract options, roster maneuvering, free agency filing — that point toward next season.
That's administrative stuff, though, and not as fun as the parade in Milwaukee — or this week, when MLB hands out its major awards in what closes the books on the 2026 season.

This year's awards week adds a new honor being handed out by the Baseball Writers' Association of America: the Reliever of the Year Award, which recognizes the top bullpen maestro from each league. Here's how this week's schedule lays out:
Wednesday: Cy Young and Reliever of the Year (7 p.m. ET, MLB Network) Thursday: MVP (7 p.m. ET, MLB Network)
MLB Network will also air the MLB awards given out during a live ceremony in Las Vegas at 8 p.m. ET on Wednesday.

Honors presented then include the Hank Aaron Award, Comeback Player of the Year, Mariano Rivera & Trevor Hoffman Relievers of the Year, Edgar Martinez Outstanding Designated Hitter Award and selections for the All-MLB first and second teams.
Finalists for the major awards have already been announced. So let's see how things look before the hardware is handed out. Who might win? Who should win?
MVP | CY Young | Reliever of the Year Rookie of the Year | Manager of the Year
Final tally: Venable 111 (15 first-place votes), Kevin Cash 98 (12), Chad Tracy 47 (3), Stephen Vogt 9, Aaron Boone 4, Joe Espada 1.

features.headline: What the Kirk Cousins trade means for the Vikings and the Raiders
features.desc: We answered big questions surrounding the trade of quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Raiders to the Vikings.
features.by: Kevin Seifert and Ryan McFadden and Jeremy Fowler and Michael F. Florio
body: Kirk Cousins played what appeared to be his final game for the Minnesota Vikings on Oct. 29, 2023.

On that afternoon at Lambeau Field, Cousins had thrown for 274 yards and two touchdowns when he tore his right Achilles tendon and was lost for the season. That moment set off a three-year odyssey that improbably ended the way it began.

Cousins returned Tuesday to the Vikings, via a trade that sent their 2027 third-round draft pick to the Las Vegas Raiders, and could start Sunday's game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field (1 p.m. ET, Fox).
Since then, the Vikings have tried eight different starting quarterbacks and made a total of 14 different in-season quarterback changes.
The most recent came Monday night at U.S. Bank Stadium, where Carson Wentz — starting in place of the injured Kyler Murray — produced the Vikings' worst game by a starting quarterback since 2006.

The Vikings have lost consecutive games after a 6-0 start, and their decision-makers did not want to waste what has been an elite-level defense and special teams performance this season with poor quarterback play.
In Las Vegas, the door is now wide open for Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 pick of the 2026 NFL draft, to step into his role as the long-term franchise quarterback.
ESPN Vikings reporter Kevin Seifert, Raiders reporter Ryan McFadden, national reporter Jeremy Fowler and fantasy's Michael F. Florio take a closer look at the questions and issues involved.
The offense under coach Kevin O'Connell has been tough for quarterbacks of all experience levels to master, and Cousins talked often in 2022 about his struggles to feel comfortable in it.

features.headline: From 2-7 to 6-2: Josh Downs reacts to Chiefs trade with Vince Carter GIF
features.desc: A moment from Vince Carter's retirement ceremony helped Downs sum up his feelings about joining Kansas City.
body: Josh Downs needed only one GIF to show how he felt about going from the 2-7 Indianapolis Colts to the 6-2 Kansas City Chiefs.

After Tuesday's trade, the wide receiver posted a popular clip of Vince Carter overcome with emotion during his Toronto Raptors jersey retirement ceremony. Often used to celebrate good news, the GIF presumably represented Downs' feelings about his new destination.

The moment dates to Nov. 2, 2024, when Carter became the first player to have his jersey retired by the Raptors. His emotional reaction as Toronto honored his No. 15 has since taken on a life of its own online.
Downs' post also caught the attention of his new quarterback, Patrick Mahomes, who reposted it with a clock emoji.

Downs, who had requested a trade, heads to Kansas City with a 2027 seventh-round pick in exchange for fourth- and fifth-round selections. He brings 33 catches for 354 yards and a touchdown this season to a Chiefs receiver group dealing with injuries to Tyquan Thornton and Xavier Worthy.
The GIF wasn't Downs' only message Tuesday. He also thanked the team that drafted him in the third round in 2023.
"I am beyond grateful and blessed for my time in Indy. Nothing but love For the Shoe," he wrote on X.

features.headline: MrBeast, meet Haaland: Man City star puts YouTuber through soccer gauntlet
features.desc: Manchester City star Erling Haaland has collaborated with popular YouTuber "MrBeast" in a series of various soccer challenges.
body: Manchester City star Erling Haaland is known for his extraordinary feats on a soccer pitch, but this time he decided to put that to the test by allowing famous YouTube star James Stephen "Jimmy" Donaldson — better known as "MrBeast"
— to participate in a series of intense soccer challenges known as the "Erling Haaland Gauntlet" at the club's training ground.

Posted on the Norway international's YouTube channel, which currently has over four million subscribers, Haaland put MrBeast — alongside his two friends Tareq Salameh and Nolan Hansen — through several soccer challenges to test their skill, strength and endurance.

The challenges consisted of sprints, wall sits, headers and a crossbar challenge, in which the winner would get a "Haaland Hammer," and the loser would have to go into goal and get hit by free shots from the penalty spot.

In the end, it was Salameh who ended up winning the "Haaland Hammer" after finishing first amongst the three, and it was MrBeast who had the misfortune of getting hit with shots from his two friends and, of course, Haaland.

It's safe to say that the most-subscribed YouTuber with over 526 million — who's known for his extraordinary challenges — probably doesn't have what it takes to cut it as a professional soccer player.

While it is currently the international break, that doesn't mean Haaland will relax while there are no matches for Manchester City. The 26-year-old was called up to play for his national team this month against Wales and Denmark in the final matches of their UEFA Nations League A campaign.
